text:
Alex P: Heads up — we're seeing a sudden drop in available GPUs in us-west2-a. ~60 GPUs moved to NotReady over the past 5m and a lot of gpu-pending pods shifted into us-west2-b. Scheduler packed the remainder oddly, now lots of tiny fragments across nodes. Anyone else seeing cross-AZ leakiness?

ops-bot: Alert: zone(us-west2-a) node-count=120 ready=60 notready=60 reason=NetworkUnavailable components=network-agent

Maria G: ugh. Can you paste `kubectl get nodes -l failure-domain=us-west2-a -o wide` and the node conditions? Might be a CNI/route flap on that AZ.

Jin S: quick dump from one affected node:
Name: gpu-node-azA-47
Labels: failure-domain=us-west2-a,gpu=true
Conditions:
  Ready: False (KubeletNotReady)
  NetworkUnavailable: True
Taints: node.kubernetes.io/network-unavailable:NoSchedule
Events: Network interface lost route to control plane at 2026-02-17T08:11:02Z

Sam R: That looks like the network-agent daemonset is failing to reconcile routes in that AZ. If nodes are tainted with network-unavailable, scheduler will avoid them and pack into the other AZs -> fragmentation. Two levers: (1) repair network-agent quickly (daemonset restart) or (2) temporarily relax topology constraints for low-priority jobs so they can backfill. Packet loss means draining will be slow.

Leah T: We should avoid mass evictions while the NICs are flaky. Suggest plan: restart network-agent on affected nodes first, then untaint nodes, then allow controlled rebalancing (drain 2-3 nodes at a time). Also consider bumping reserved capacity for critical GPU workloads so autoscaler doesn't overreact.

Maria G: Command to restart network-agent daemonset (canary first):
kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/network-agent --selector=failure-domain=us-west2-a
kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=network-agent -o wide

deploy-bot: Started rollout restart for daemonset/network-agent in namespace infra (selector=failure-domain=us-west2-a) — 3/120 updated (canary).

Alex P: I'll hold on mass drains. If restart fixes routes, nodes should recover and scheduler will stop overpacking other AZ. If not, we may need to temporarily lift `topologySpreadConstraints` for best-effort training jobs to reduce tail latency on serving.

Jin S: For monitoring: watch `kubelet_runtime_operations` and `node_network_up` and GPU allocatable metrics. Also check binpacking heatmap: `./tools/binpack-heatmap --zone us-west2` — if there are many nodes with <0.2 GPU allocable left, we'll be fragmented.

Sam R: Also note cost impact: when pods spike into another AZ we incur cross-AZ egress and potential overprovisioning. Keep finance in the loop if this persists >2h.

Maria G: If network-agent restart doesn't clear within 10m, plan B is to cordon the worst nodes and migrate small noncritical pods manually using `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` in small batches. Avoid draining GPU-heavy model-serving pods during business hours.

ops-bot: Monitoring snapshot: network-agent crashloop count in us-west2-a = 18, node_recover_rate = 0.1/min.

Alex P: Update: canary restart looks good on 3 nodes, routes restored. Rolling restart proceeding. Will re-evaluate fragmentation in 15m and post heatmap. Thanks all — leaning on ops runbook now. :thumbsup: 

Leah T: Thanks — ping me if drains are needed, I can coordinate with SRE to throttle.

Maria G: Good catch, Alex. Once stable let's talk about a scheduler tweak to prefer spreading by `gpu_sku` label not just zone — that might reduce micro-fragmentation next time.

Alex P: Agreed. Follow-up: file a short postmortem with root cause pinned to network-agent route reconciliation in that AZ and include mitigation (canary rollout pattern + quick untaint playbook).
